title: Isaiah Chapter 61 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Isaiah chapter 61 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Isaiah Chapter 61 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Isaiah Chapter 61.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 61:1, who is upon the speaker?
options: The Spirit of the Lord GOD
The angel of the LORD
The Holy Spirit
The prophet Elijah
questions.correctAnswer: The Spirit of the Lord GOD
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:1 states, 'The Spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me,' indicating the Spirit of the Lord GOD is upon the speaker.

questions.question: In Isaiah 61:1, what has the LORD anointed the speaker to do?
options: To preach good tidings unto the meek
To build a temple
To lead an army
To write the law
questions.correctAnswer: To preach good tidings unto the meek
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:1 says, 'because the LORD hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek,' showing the speaker's purpose.

questions.question: What is the speaker sent to do besides preach good tidings in Isaiah 61:1?
options: To bind up the brokenhearted and proclaim liberty to captives
To build a city
To judge the nations
To write psalms
questions.correctAnswer: To bind up the brokenhearted and proclaim liberty to captives
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:1 states the speaker is sent 'to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives.'

questions.question: What does Isaiah 61:2 say the speaker is to proclaim?
options: The acceptable year of the LORD and the day of vengeance of our God
The coming of a king
The building of the temple
The laws of Moses
questions.correctAnswer: The acceptable year of the LORD and the day of vengeance of our God
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:2 explicitly mentions proclaiming 'the acceptable year of the LORD, and the day of vengeance of our God.'

questions.question: According to Isaiah 61:2, whom is the speaker to comfort?
options: All that mourn
The kings
The priests
The merchants
questions.correctAnswer: All that mourn
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:2 ends with 'to comfort all that mourn,' indicating the speaker’s mission.

questions.question: What will be given to those who mourn in Zion according to Isaiah 61:3?
options: Beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness
Gold and silver
A new temple
Food and drink
questions.correctAnswer: Beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:3 describes giving 'beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness.'

questions.question: What will those who mourn in Zion be called, as stated in Isaiah 61:3?
options: Trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD
Kings and priests
Children of the exile
Servants of the temple
questions.correctAnswer: Trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:3 says they 'might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD.'

questions.question: What will they do to the old wastes and former desolations according to Isaiah 61:4?
options: Build them up and repair waste cities
Destroy them completely
Leave them as they are
Turn them into gardens
questions.correctAnswer: Build them up and repair waste cities
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:4 states, 'they shall build the old wastes... and they shall repair the waste cities.'

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 61:1 mentions the speaker is sent to open the prison to those bound.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:1 explicitly says the speaker is sent 'to the opening of the prison to them that are bound.'

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 61:2 only mentions comforting kings and priests.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:2 says 'to comfort all that mourn,' not specifically kings or priests.

questions.question: In Isaiah 61, which comes first?
options: Binding up the brokenhearted
Building old wastes
Comforting all that mourn
Being called trees of righteousness
questions.correctAnswer: Binding up the brokenhearted
questions.explanation: Binding up the brokenhearted is mentioned first in verse 1 before the other listed events in later verses.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 61:4 mentions repairing desolations of many generations.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:4 says they 'shall repair the waste cities, the desolations of many generations.'

questions.question: According to Isaiah 61:3, what is given for mourning?
options: The oil of joy
A crown of gold
A new home
A feast
questions.correctAnswer: The oil of joy
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:3 states 'the oil of joy for mourning' is given.

questions.question: Who does Isaiah 61:4 say will raise up the former desolations?
options: They (the people)
The angels
The kings
The prophets
questions.correctAnswer: They (the people)
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:4 says 'they shall raise up the former desolations,' referring to the people being described.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 61:3 says those who mourn will be called the planting of the LORD.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:3 says those who mourn 'might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD.'

medium.title: Isaiah Chapter 61 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Isaiah Chapter 61 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 61:5, who will tend your flocks and work your fields?
options: Strangers and sons of aliens
Your own family members
The priests of the LORD
The captives and prisoners
questions.correctAnswer: Strangers and sons of aliens
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:5 states that strangers shall stand and feed your flocks, and the sons of the alien shall be your plowmen and vinedressers, indicating that foreign people will help cultivate and tend your lands.

questions.question: What new name and role does Isaiah 61:6 say the people will receive?
options: Priests of the LORD and Ministers of God
Kings and Rulers of the earth
Prophets and Seers
Shepherds and Farmers
questions.correctAnswer: Priests of the LORD and Ministers of God
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:6 declares that the people shall be named the Priests of the LORD and called Ministers of God, signifying a sacred role and identity among the nations.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 61:7 describe the blessing for those who experienced shame and confusion?
options: They will receive double and everlasting joy
They will be forgotten and ignored
They will suffer more shame
They will be taken captive again
questions.correctAnswer: They will receive double and everlasting joy
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:7 promises that for shame, the people will have double, and for confusion, they will rejoice in their portion, possessing double in their land with everlasting joy.

questions.question: What does the LORD say He hates and loves according to Isaiah 61:8?
options: Hates robbery for burnt offering; loves judgment
Hates prayer; loves sacrifice
Hates strangers; loves the poor
Hates fasting; loves offerings
questions.correctAnswer: Hates robbery for burnt offering; loves judgment
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:8 clearly states that the LORD loves judgment and hates robbery for burnt offering, emphasizing His preference for justice over empty rituals.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 61:6, what will the people eat and boast in?
options: The riches and glory of the Gentiles
The fruits of their own labor
Forbidden food
The offerings made by strangers
questions.correctAnswer: The riches and glory of the Gentiles
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:6 indicates that the people shall eat the riches of the Gentiles and boast in their glory, showing a reversal of fortunes where God's people will enjoy abundance.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 61:5 describe the foreigners' roles in the community?
options: Feeding flocks and working as plowmen and vinedressers
Leading worship and teaching the law
Building walls and repairing cities
Serving as judges and rulers
questions.correctAnswer: Feeding flocks and working as plowmen and vinedressers
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly says strangers will feed flocks and sons of aliens will be plowmen and vinedressers, showing their involvement in agricultural labor.

questions.question: What will the LORD do according to Isaiah 61:8 after expressing His hatred for robbery in burnt offerings?
options: Direct their work in truth and make an everlasting covenant
Punish the wicked and destroy the sinners
Send prophets to call for repentance
Remove the people from the land
questions.correctAnswer: Direct their work in truth and make an everlasting covenant
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:8 reveals God's intentions to guide their work in truth and establish an everlasting covenant with them, highlighting His faithfulness and righteous governance.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 61:7 imply will replace shame and confusion?
options: Double joy and possession of land
Continued suffering and exile
Silence and despair
Loss of all possessions
questions.correctAnswer: Double joy and possession of land
questions.explanation: The verse promises that shame and confusion will be replaced by double blessings and everlasting joy in their land, affirming restoration and celebration.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 61:9 says the seed of God's people will be ignored and forgotten among the Gentiles.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:9 states the opposite; it says their seed shall be known among the Gentiles and acknowledged as blessed by the LORD, indicating honor and recognition.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 61:6 suggest believers should view their identity and role?
options: As priests and ministers of God who will enjoy Gentile riches
As servants obligated to foreign rulers
As outcasts without inheritance
As silent observers of God’s plans
questions.correctAnswer: As priests and ministers of God who will enjoy Gentile riches
questions.explanation: The verse calls believers priests and ministers of the LORD who will partake in the riches of the Gentiles, encouraging a confident, honored identity.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 61:5 instruct about trusting others with your resources?
options: Trust strangers and aliens to help with your flocks and fields
Only family members should care for your resources
Avoid sharing your land with outsiders
Hire only priests to manage your property
questions.correctAnswer: Trust strangers and aliens to help with your flocks and fields
questions.explanation: The verse encourages openness to receiving help from strangers and aliens in agricultural work, showing trust and inclusion in provision.

questions.question: Context question: What does Isaiah 61:7 promise will happen if you accept the new identity as Priests of the LORD described in Isaiah 61:6?
options: You will receive double blessings and everlasting joy
You will be rejected by all nations
You will remain in shame and confusion
You will lose your land
questions.correctAnswer: You will receive double blessings and everlasting joy
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:6 speaks of being named priests and ministers, and Isaiah 61:7 builds on this by promising double blessings and everlasting joy to those who embrace this identity.

questions.question: Context question: According to Isaiah 61:8, what is the result of the LORD loving judgment and hating robbery for burnt offering as introduced in the same verse?
options: He will direct their work in truth and establish an everlasting covenant
He will destroy the wicked without mercy
He will allow injustice to prevail
He will reject the people and abandon them
questions.correctAnswer: He will direct their work in truth and establish an everlasting covenant
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:8 links God's love for judgment and hatred of robbery to His promise to lead the people's work in truth and set an everlasting covenant, showing the connection between justice and covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 61:5 suggests that foreigners will be excluded from participating in the community's agriculture.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:5 says that strangers and sons of aliens will feed flocks and be plowmen and vinedressers, indicating inclusion rather than exclusion.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 61:8 tells us that God will make an everlasting covenant with His people and guide their work in truth.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:8 explicitly states God will direct their work in truth and make an everlasting covenant with them, affirming His enduring commitment and guidance.

hard.title: Isaiah Chapter 61 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Isaiah Chapter 61.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 61:9, how will the seed and offspring be recognized among the Gentiles?
options: They will be feared and avoided
They will be known and acknowledged as blessed by the LORD
They will be enslaved by the Gentiles
They will be forgotten and scattered
questions.correctAnswer: They will be known and acknowledged as blessed by the LORD
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:9 states that their seed shall be known among the Gentiles and their offspring among the people; all that see them shall acknowledge them as the seed which the LORD hath blessed.

questions.question: In Isaiah 61:10, what garments is the speaker clothed with as a symbol of salvation and righteousness?
options: The mantle of prophecy and the sash of peace
The garments of salvation and the robe of righteousness
The armor of God and the helmet of salvation
The priestly ephod and the sash of holiness
questions.correctAnswer: The garments of salvation and the robe of righteousness
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:10 describes being clothed with the garments of salvation and covered with the robe of righteousness, symbolizing divine blessing and deliverance.

questions.question: What metaphor does Isaiah 61:10 use to describe the joy and adornment associated with righteousness?
options: A warrior’s shield and helmet
A king’s crown and scepter
A bridegroom decked with ornaments and a bride adorned with jewels
A shepherd’s staff and cloak
questions.correctAnswer: A bridegroom decked with ornaments and a bride adorned with jewels
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:10 uses the metaphor of a bridegroom decorating himself with ornaments and a bride adorning herself with jewels to describe the joyous adornment of righteousness.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 61:11 describe the Lord GOD’s work of righteousness and praise among the nations?
options: Like a storm that scatters the wicked
Like a mountain that stands forever
Like the earth bringing forth buds and a garden causing seeds to spring forth
Like a river that dries up in the desert
questions.correctAnswer: Like the earth bringing forth buds and a garden causing seeds to spring forth
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:11 compares the growth of righteousness and praise to the natural and fruitful processes of the earth bringing forth buds and a garden causing seeds to spring forth.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage is closely connected to the opening of Isaiah 61, where the Spirit of the LORD anoints to preach good tidings to the meek?
options: Matthew 5:1-12 (The Beatitudes)
Luke 4:18-19 (Jesus reads Isaiah 61 in the synagogue)
John 3:16 (God’s love for the world)
Acts 2:1-4 (Pentecost)
questions.correctAnswer: Luke 4:18-19 (Jesus reads Isaiah 61 in the synagogue)
questions.explanation: Luke 4:18-19 records Jesus reading Isaiah 61:1-2 and declaring its fulfillment in Himself, directly connecting Isaiah 61’s theme of anointing and mission with the New Testament.

questions.question: In Isaiah 61:8, the LORD declares His love for which concept and hatred for what kind of offering?
options: Love for mercy; hatred for burnt offerings
Love for judgment; hatred for robbery for burnt offering
Love for sacrifice; hatred for prayer without deeds
Love for faithfulness; hatred for idolatry
questions.correctAnswer: Love for judgment; hatred for robbery for burnt offering
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:8 states that the LORD loves judgment and hates robbery for burnt offering, emphasizing His desire for justice over empty ritual.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 61:7, what will be given in place of shame and confusion for those who mourn?
options: Peace and silence
Double portion and everlasting joy
Wealth and power
Wisdom and long life
questions.correctAnswer: Double portion and everlasting joy
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:7 promises that for shame there will be double, and for confusion they shall rejoice in their portion, with everlasting joy given to them.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 61:6 says that those called the Priests of the LORD will eat the riches of the Gentiles and boast in their glory.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:6 explicitly states that those named the Priests of the LORD will eat the riches of the Gentiles and in their glory boast themselves.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Isaiah 61:3 when it mentions 'beauty for ashes,' 'oil of joy for mourning,' and 'garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness'?
options: Chiasm
Parallelism
Metaphor
Alliteration
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:3 employs parallelism, a common Hebrew poetic device, by pairing contrasting images to emphasize transformation and restoration.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word translated as 'anointed' in Isaiah 61:1 signify in the original context?
options: To be chosen or consecrated for a divine purpose
To be healed or made whole
To be taught or instructed
To be judged or condemned
questions.correctAnswer: To be chosen or consecrated for a divine purpose
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'anointed' (mashach) means to be chosen or consecrated for a special divine mission, highlighting the speaker’s God-ordained role in Isaiah 61:1.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage shares a thematic connection with Isaiah 61:11’s imagery of the earth bringing forth her bud and the garden causing things to spring forth?
options: Psalm 1:3 (The righteous as a flourishing tree)
Genesis 1:11-12 (Creation of vegetation)
Jeremiah 17:7-8 (Blessed man like a tree planted by water)
All of the above
questions.correctAnswer: All of the above
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:11’s imagery resonates with Psalm 1:3, Genesis 1:11-12, and Jeremiah 17:7-8, all of which use natural growth metaphors to express blessing, righteousness, and divine favor.

questions.question: Historically, what was the significance of proclaiming the 'acceptable year of the LORD' as mentioned in Isaiah 61:2?
options: It referred to the weekly Sabbath rest
It was linked to the Jubilee year when debts were forgiven and captives freed
It was a festival celebrating the harvest
It was a royal coronation event
questions.correctAnswer: It was linked to the Jubilee year when debts were forgiven and captives freed
questions.explanation: The 'acceptable year of the LORD' in Isaiah 61:2 alludes to the Jubilee year described in Leviticus 25, a time of liberation and restoration in ancient Israel.

questions.question: Which New Testament letter echoes the theme of being clothed with righteousness similar to Isaiah 61:10?
options: Romans 13:14
Ephesians 6:11
Galatians 3:27
Hebrews 4:16
questions.correctAnswer: Galatians 3:27
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:27 speaks of being clothed with Christ, echoing the Isaiah 61:10 imagery of being clothed with salvation and righteousness.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 61:4 predicts that the people will rebuild the old wastes and repair the desolations of many generations.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:4 states this rebuilding and repair, but since the focus of the quiz is on the final third of the chapter where this promise is not repeated, this question references an earlier verse and is false for the purpose of no verse repetition.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 61:9's promise of the seed being known among the Gentiles relate to the New Testament concept of the inclusion of Gentiles in God's covenant?
options: It contradicts the New Testament by excluding Gentiles
It foreshadows the New Testament teaching of Gentile inclusion in Romans and Ephesians
It only applies to Old Testament Israel with no New Testament relevance
It refers solely to physical descendants without spiritual meaning
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows the New Testament teaching of Gentile inclusion in Romans and Ephesians
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:9’s promise anticipates the inclusion of Gentiles into God's covenant people, a theme fully developed in New Testament books like Romans 11 and Ephesians 2.

theological.title: Isaiah Chapter 61 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Isaiah Chapter 61 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 61:1, what is the primary mission given by the LORD to the anointed one?
options: To preach good tidings to the meek and bind up the brokenhearted
To call down fire from heaven upon the enemies
To establish a political kingdom on earth
To gather Israel from all nations
questions.correctAnswer: To preach good tidings to the meek and bind up the brokenhearted
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:1 clearly states that the Spirit of the Lord anointed the speaker to preach good tidings to the meek and to bind up the brokenhearted, highlighting the mission of restoration and comfort.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 61:2 reveal about the dual nature of God's work in this chapter?
options: It involves both proclaiming liberty and executing vengeance
It focuses solely on comfort without judgment
It emphasizes only the rebuilding of physical cities
It calls for silence in the face of injustice
questions.correctAnswer: It involves both proclaiming liberty and executing vengeance
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:2 mentions the acceptable year of the LORD and the day of vengeance of God, revealing a balance between mercy and judgment within God's redemptive work.

questions.question: Which doctrine is illustrated by the promise in Isaiah 61:3 about exchanging mourning for joy and praise?
options: Sanctification and restoration through God’s grace
Predestination based on human works
The cessation of sorrow in the present age
The inevitability of physical resurrection
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification and restoration through God’s grace
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:3 describes God giving beauty for ashes, oil of joy for mourning, and a garment of praise for heaviness, illustrating the doctrine of sanctification and restoration by divine grace.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 61:4, what is the theological significance of rebuilding the old wastes and raising up former desolations?
options: It symbolizes God's covenant faithfulness and the restoration of His people
It shows the futility of human efforts apart from God
It predicts the physical destruction of Jerusalem
It commands immediate military conquest
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes God's covenant faithfulness and the restoration of His people
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:4 speaks of rebuilding and repairing desolations, symbolizing God’s faithfulness to restore His covenant people and their land, a key theme in biblical theology.

questions.question: What attribute of God is primarily demonstrated in Isaiah 61:8 where the LORD declares He loves judgment and hates robbery for burnt offering?
options: God’s justice and righteousness
God’s wrath exclusively
God’s indifference
God’s favoritism
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice and righteousness
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:8 explicitly states God’s love for judgment and hatred of false offerings, revealing His attribute of perfect justice and righteousness.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 61:6 reveal the future role of God’s people in relation to the Gentiles?
options: They shall be priests and ministers, and eat the riches of the Gentiles
They shall be conquered and enslaved by the Gentiles
They shall worship Gentile gods
They shall be isolated from the Gentiles
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be priests and ministers, and eat the riches of the Gentiles
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:6 states that God’s people will be called priests and ministers and will enjoy the riches of the Gentiles, indicating a sanctified role and blessing among nations.

questions.question: What combined theological truth is conveyed by Isaiah 61:7 and Isaiah 61:9 about the blessings for God's people?
options: They will receive double joy and be recognized among the Gentiles as blessed by the LORD
They will suffer eternal shame and be forgotten
They will be destroyed and their offspring scattered
They will lose their identity and be assimilated
questions.correctAnswer: They will receive double joy and be recognized among the Gentiles as blessed by the LORD
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:7 promises double joy replacing shame, and Isaiah 61:9 says their seed will be known among Gentiles as blessed by the LORD, together teaching restoration and divine favor.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 61:10 teach about the spiritual significance of salvation and righteousness?
options: Salvation and righteousness are like garments adorning the believer
Salvation is temporary and easily lost
Righteousness is self-earned by human effort
Salvation excludes joy and rejoicing
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation and righteousness are like garments adorning the believer
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:10 uses the metaphor of clothing to describe salvation and righteousness, emphasizing their role as divine gifts that spiritually adorn and transform the believer.

questions.question: What broader redemptive narrative is Isaiah 61:11 connecting to through the imagery of the earth bringing forth buds and gardens yielding growth?
options: God’s promise of new creation and global righteousness
The immediate restoration of only Israel’s physical land
The end of the agricultural cycle
The destruction of all nations
questions.correctAnswer: God’s promise of new creation and global righteousness
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:11 uses creation imagery to symbolize the unfolding of God’s redemptive plan culminating in worldwide righteousness and praise, tying into biblical new creation themes (Revelation 21:1).

questions.question: How does the promise in Isaiah 61:5 about strangers feeding your flocks and aliens serving as plowmen relate to biblical theology of Gentile inclusion?
options: It anticipates Gentile participation in God’s covenant blessings
It predicts Gentile domination over Israel with no blessing
It excludes Gentiles from all spiritual benefits
It commands Israel to reject foreigners entirely
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates Gentile participation in God’s covenant blessings
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:5 shows Gentiles serving and aiding God’s people, prefiguring the inclusion of Gentiles into God’s covenant blessings and kingdom purposes (cf. Romans 11:17-24).

questions.question: What doctrine concerning God’s covenantal faithfulness is taught by the promise of an everlasting covenant in Isaiah 61:8?
options: God establishes an unbreakable relationship with His people based on truth
God’s covenant depends on human perfection
God’s covenant is temporary and conditional
God’s covenant is limited to physical descendants only
questions.correctAnswer: God establishes an unbreakable relationship with His people based on truth
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:8 declares God will make an everlasting covenant and direct their work in truth, teaching the doctrine of God’s unchanging, faithful covenantal relationship.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Isaiah 61:1 and Isaiah 61:11 convey about the Spirit’s role in the mission and outcome of God's work?
options: The Spirit anoints for preaching and causes righteousness to spring forth globally
The Spirit is silent and inactive in the world
The Spirit condemns without offering restoration
The Spirit focuses only on Israel’s national restoration
questions.correctAnswer: The Spirit anoints for preaching and causes righteousness to spring forth globally
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:1 shows the Spirit anointing for proclamation, while 61:11 reveals God causing righteousness and praise to spring forth, teaching the Spirit’s integral role in mission and universal redemption.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Isaiah 61:1-3 is merely a promise to Israel's earthly restoration with no messianic significance. What does Isaiah 61:1-3 actually teach about the nature of this anointed mission?
options: It prophesies a messianic mission to bring spiritual freedom, healing, and universal praise
It only refers to a political leader rebuilding Jerusalem
It promises only temporal prosperity with no spiritual dimension
It forbids any proclamation to the meek
questions.correctAnswer: It prophesies a messianic mission to bring spiritual freedom, healing, and universal praise
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:1-3 describes the Spirit-anointed one preaching good tidings, binding broken hearts, proclaiming liberty, and bringing praise, which Christian theology interprets as messianic prophecy fulfilled in Christ (Luke 4:18-19).

questions.question: What doctrine regarding the identity and blessing of God's people is revealed by Isaiah 61:9?
options: God’s people are recognized among the nations as His blessed seed
God’s people are hidden and unknown among the nations
God’s people lose their blessing when scattered
God’s people are cursed by the Gentiles
questions.correctAnswer: God’s people are recognized among the nations as His blessed seed
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:9 teaches that the seed of God’s people will be known and acknowledged among the Gentiles as blessed by the LORD, affirming their identity and blessing in the nations.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 61:10 reflect the attribute of God related to salvation?
options: God’s saving work adorns believers with righteousness and joy
God’s salvation is hidden and causes sorrow
God’s salvation is based on human merit
God’s salvation removes the need for righteousness
questions.correctAnswer: God’s saving work adorns believers with righteousness and joy
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:10 celebrates God clothing the speaker with garments of salvation and robes of righteousness, showing God’s gracious saving work that brings joy and spiritual adornment.
